source_snapshot.procedure: Enable EDKII debug/WHEA controls, boot Windows with Intel ITP, halt, run `ei.injectI3CControllerError(socket=0, lpss=0, errType=0x13)`, then resume.
source_snapshot.criteria: System hangs; BMC and optional UEFI record a catastrophic or misspelled `fater` error; front-panel light turns on; optional LCD displays catastrophic/fater information.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; FAE owns injection and agent attempts host dmesg plus BMC SEL capture.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CHANGED with socket/errType approval, hang recovery, physical evidence and restoration.

historical_reviews.deepseek: The post-event SSH plan is incompatible with the required system hang and cannot prove exact controller ownership, socket coverage or recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly gates the fatal injection but assumes the Intel LPSS path without applying the project I3C ownership rule or resolving socket 0~N versus hardcoded socket 0.
historical_reviews.related_cases: No adjacent ADDDC or leaky-bucket evidence can substitute for I3C controller ownership and hang behavior.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Wistron I3C defaults to BMC/platform-management scope unless a platform specification explicitly authorizes another ownership path.

original_test_intent: Inject the approved I3C controller error on every supported socket/controller target and verify a deliberate hang with the platform-defined catastrophic/fatal BMC, UEFI, front-panel and LCD response, followed by bounded recovery.
original_method: The platform owner first proves I3C ownership, maps sockets to controller/LPSS instances and defines error code 0x13. A qualified FAE runs one injection per approved target with an armed OOB console and timer; an independent observer captures the hang and management-plane indications, then performs the approved recovery and restores settings.
manual_activity: The FAE must confirm the ownership exception, enable debug controls, inject one approved target and operate recovery. A separate observer must time the hang and capture front-panel/LCD evidence because the host is expected to become unreachable.
required_inputs: Platform specification proving Intel/host LPSS I3C ownership or identifying the BMC/OOB controller instead
Socket 0~N to controller/LPSS/bus/endpoint map and coverage sequence
Maximum hang duration, exact catastrophic/fatal event codes and indicator/LCD applicability
Independent OOB console, backup, reset/recovery and BIOS restoration plan
safety_requirements: Dedicated idle SUT with stable power and independent BMC/serial observer
Do not treat a host-side LPSS injector as valid without explicit platform ownership proof
Run one mapped target at a time with a hard hang timeout and armed recovery
Stop on wrong controller, unexpected severity, missing management evidence or failed recovery
Never retry or reset autonomously; preserve evidence before recovery
agent_execution_scope: Validate owner-supplied topology/ownership and collect reachable read-only pre-state plus independent OOB/BMC evidence
Do not select socket/LPSS/error type, alter BIOS, inject, reset/retry or set PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Resolve I3C ownership and socket/controller map
Define hang/fatal event/indicator/LCD oracle and timing

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Host SSH/dmesg cannot be the primary post-check when the expected outcome is a hang; BMC collection must use an independent OOB path and UEFI evidence is recovered afterward.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run the literal socket=0/lpss=0/0x13 command only if the platform spec maps that target; define additional real commands for Socket 1~N rather than extrapolating.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The I3C controller-error stimulus, 0x13 source value, deliberate hang and 30/30-minute estimates are retained, but target expansion is not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Time-synchronize ITP, serial console and BMC event streaming, inject one mapped target, measure loss of host progress/heartbeat, capture exact management events and indicators, recover at the approved deadline, collect UEFI logs and verify restored health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes a hang objectively observable without relying on the hung host and enforces the Wistron I3C ownership rule.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An `i3c` keyword after reboot cannot prove which controller was injected, when the host hung or whether the required catastrophic path occurred.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong controller or unbounded fatal injection can sever management access, corrupt active work or leave the SUT unrecoverable.

project_override_considerations: I3C is BMC/platform-management scope by default in this project. The Intel LPSS method requires an explicit platform-spec exception identifying controller, bus, endpoint and expected response; otherwise execution must remain stopped.
expected_evidence: Approved ownership specification and SUT/socket/controller/LPSS/bus identity
Package hash, mapping matrix, exact commands and 0x13 definition
Pre/post BIOS settings and complete ITP transcript
Independent console hang timeline plus BMC/UEFI event codes and front-panel/LCD evidence
Recovery/reset transcript, restored health/settings and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items requires Socket 0~N but the only command hardcodes socket=0/lpss=0; I3C ownership conflicts with the project BMC default unless explicitly overridden; 0x13 and `fater` are undefined; Windows conflicts with dmesg; and host SSH collection is infeasible during the required hang.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intended I3C fatal-path test is understandable and can be safely parameterized by the platform owner. Missing ownership, map and recovery block execution, not completion of this static review.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 28 Wistron-System RAS-00748-V003: provide the platform-spec exception proving Intel LPSS rather than project-default BMC I3C ownership, Socket 0~N to LPSS/bus/endpoint mapping and commands, ITP/CScripts version/hash and errType 0x13 meaning; define maximum hang, exact catastrophic/fatal BMC/UEFI/front-panel/LCD oracle, independent OOB evidence and reset/recovery/restoration.

review_improvement: Replaces impossible post-hang host polling with independent OOB evidence and prevents a CPU-side injector from silently violating the project's I3C ownership rule.
independent_technical_reasoning: A deliberate hang removes the host as a reliable observer, so the acceptance path must be built around an independent console and BMC event source. The source also claims all sockets while invoking only socket 0/lpss 0, and Wistron policy treats I3C as management-owned unless a supplied specification says otherwise. Those are execution-critical identity issues, but the intended fatal-controller-error scenario remains identifiable. With an owner-approved exception, target matrix and recovery timer, the case is RPUC rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.
